Diastereoselective Addition of Lithiated Allenyl Sulfones to
Nonracemic Sulfinimines: Asymmetric Synthesis of Diverse
Heterocycles
Mahesh S. Gadhave and Kavirayani R. Prasad*
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2024, 89, 15364−15373

ABSTRACT: The addition of lithiated allenyl sulfones to nonracemic
sulfinimines furnished sulfinamides possessing the allenyl sulfonyl moiety
with excellent diastereoselectivity. The formed products are transformed into
different heterocycles, including the synthesis of pyrroline, pyran, and
functionalized benzopyran.
N
onracemic sulfinimines developed by Davis and Ellman
are widely used building blocks for the synthesis of chiral
amine-containing compounds.
1
With the consistently high
diastereoselectivities realized in the addition of nucleophiles to
the sulfinimines and the ease of removal of the sulfinyl group, the
sulfinimines have been widely used in the asymmetric synthesis
of nitrogen-containing compounds. While a plethora of
nucleophilic addition reactions of sulfinimines have been
reported in the literature, the addition of simple metalated
allenes to sulfinimines has been studied less frequently. The
addition of simple allenylzinc bromide or allenyl lithium
reagents to sulfinimines always produced the corresponding
homopropargyl amines.
2
Although there has been one report of
the addition of lithiated sulfonyl allenes to p-toluenesulfonyl
imines (Scheme 1, eq a), there has been no report on the
asymmetric addition to sulfinimines or imines.
3
We reasoned
that the lithiation of allenyl sulfone 1 should lead to lithiated
allene 1a
4
stabilized by the directing sulfonyl group that upon
addition to nonracemic sulfinimines should form the allene-
containing sulfinamides (Scheme 1, eq b) in an asymmetric
fashion. Allenes containing the amine/hydroxy tether are proven
substrates for the synthesis of several heterocyclic compounds.
5
Accordingly, the investigations commenced with the addition
of lithiated sulfonyl allene 1a (prepared by reaction of 1 with
LiHMDS) to sulfinimine 2a obtained from benzaldehyde. It was
found that the reaction of sulfone 1 with sulfinimine 2a in the
presence of 1.2 equiv of LiHMDS furnished product 3a in 83%
yield with a >99:1 diastereomeric ratio after column
chromatography. It is important to note that the addition of
lithiated allene devoid of the methyl groups to 2a was messy,
with no appreciable formation of any characterizable product.
Generalization of the reaction with the addition of lithiated
allene 1 to several sulfinimines prepared from various aryl
aldehydes was undertaken. Thus, addition of 1 to sulfinimine 2b
derived from 2-bromo benzaldehyde gave product 3b with
excellent diastereoselectivity in good yields. The addition of
allene 1 to sulfinimine 2c derived from 2-OMe benzaldehyde
afforded a separable mixture of diastereomers 3c and 3c′ in 69%
and 4% yields, respectively, while the addition to sulfinimine 2d
obtained from 2-tert-butyl-dimethylsilyloxy benzaldehyde pro-
duced a separable mixture of diastereomers 3d and 3d′ in 25%
and 7% yields, respectively. Addition to sulfinimines 2e−g
obtained from 3-OMe benzaldehyde, 4-OMe benzaldehyde, and
4-Cl benzaldehyde furnished allenyl sulfinamides 3e−g,
respectively, in good yields with good to excellent diastereo-
meric ratios. Addition of 1 to sulfinimine 2h obtained from 4-
nitro benzaldehyde produced product 3h in 42% yield (dr
>99:1). Reaction of 1 with sulfinimine 2i−k prepared from
heteroatom-containing aromatic aldehydes such as 2-thienyl-
carboxaldehyde, 3-furancarboxaldehyde, and N-Boc indole-3-
carboxaldehyde furnished products 3i (dr 94:6), 3j (dr 94:6),
and 3k (dr 76:24, nonseparable) in 75%, 81%, and 87% yields,

cinnamaldehyde afforded product 3l as a nonseparable mixture
(dr 80:20) in 82% yield, while reaction with sulfinimine 2m
obtained from crotonaldehyde afforded a separable mixture of
diastereomers 3m and 3m′ in 28% and 7% yields, respectively.
However, reaction with sulfinimine 2n prepared from 3-
methylcrotonaldehyde furnished major diastereomer 3n in
66% yield, while minor diastereomer 3n′ was isolated in 11%
yield. The stereochemistry of the formed products was further
confirmed by X-ray crystal structure analysis of compound 3f.
6
After the addition of allene 1 with sulfinimines derived from
aromatic aldehydes and unsaturated aldehydes was established,
the reaction with sulfinimines prepared from aliphatic aldehydes
was investigated. The reaction of 1 with sulfinimine 3o derived
from acetaldehyde furnished the product in 35% yield (dr
>99:1), while the reaction with isobutyraldehyde 3p afforded
the major diastereomer in 40% yield after chromatography.
7

product in 23% yield, while the minor product was isolated in 6%
yield. Addition to sulfinimine 2r obtained from benzyloxyace-
taldehyde furnished allene 3r as a nonseparable 90:10 mixture of
diastereomers. The reaction with sulfinimine 2s prepared from
3-tert-butyldimethylsilyloxy propanaldehyde afforded product
3s as the major diastereomer in 66% yield. Addition of 1 to
sulfinimine 2t prepared from 4-bromo-butanal directly
produced sulfinamido pyrrolidine 3t in 61% yield. However,
the reaction of sulfinimine 2u prepared from 5-bromo-pentanal
afforded a mixture of intermediate sulfinamide and cyclic
sulfinamido piperidine 3u, which was cumbersome to purify. To
overcome this difficulty, the product obtained after the addition
of 1 to imine 2u was treated with NaH to afford sulfinamido
piperidine 3u in 49% yield with a >99:1 diastereomeric ratio
(Scheme-2). It is evident from the crystal structure analysis that
the addition of a nucleophile is taking place from a side opposite
that of the sulfinyl oxygen. This can be explained by a
nonchelation model proposed earlier by Davis
8a
for the addition
of organozinc reagents to sulfinimines and by us in our earlier
studies concerning the addition of bulky nucleophiles to
sulfinimines (Fig. 1 in Scheme 2).
8b,c
The utility of the formed sulfinamido allenes in the synthesis
of diverse heterocycles was demonstrated by the following
transformations. The reaction of 3a with AgNO
3
gave
substituted sulfinamido pyrroline 4 in 77% yield.
3
Treatment
of 4 with ethereal HCl cleanly removed the sulfinyl group to
afford pyrroline 4a in 84% yield. However, attempted
deprotection of the sulfinyl group in allene 3a was not clean
and produced an array of noncharacterizable products.
Desilylation of 3s with TBAF not only deprotected the silylether
but also led to an intramolecular Michael addition to afford
substituted tetrahydropyran 5 in 73% yield. A similar outcome
was observed in the reaction of 3d with TBAF to afford
substituted benzopyran 6 in 99% yield (Scheme 3).
9
In conclusion, the diastereoselective addition of lithiated
sulfonyl allenes to nonracemic sulfinimines was developed. The
reaction was found to be general, and sulfinimines prepared from
aromatic, aliphatic, and unsaturated aldehydes provided the
products with good to excellent diastereomeric ratios and yields.
The utility of the formed products was exemplified in the
synthesis of diverse heterocycles such as functionalized
pyrroline, pyran, and benzopyran.
■
